top_temples.name: Shakti Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Upper Bazar / Zarkawt area of Aizawl; one of the city's better-known Hindu shrines.

top_temples.name: Shiv Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Armed Veng Rd, Aizawl; neighborhood temple in a residential part of the city.

top_temples.name: OM Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Aizawl 796017; known locally as a quiet spot for prayer and meditation.

top_temples.name: Assam Rifles Mandir (Hari Mandir)
top_temples.location_note: Khatla/Canteen Square, Aizawl; maintained by Assam Rifles for over 70 years, serving Gorkha Hindu and Bru Reang communities; was in the news in 2024-25 over a planned relocation.

top_temples.name: Shri Radha Krishna Temple
top_temples.location_note: Tuivamit, near Solomon's Temple Rd, Aizawl.

top_temples.name: Vishwakarma Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Lawngtlai town; a small, single-storey shrine serving the local craftsmen/artisan community.

top_temples.name: Rama Mandir
top_temples.location_note: On a hill overlooking Lunglei town; simple white structure with a sloping roof in the local Mizo style, reached via a steep climb.

top_temples.name: Sarvajanin Temple
top_temples.location_note: Assam Rifles Complex, Saihatlangkawn Road, Saiha.

top_temples.name: Kali Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Saiha town; concrete construction with an orange facade, associated with the local Bengali and Marwari Hindu community, said to date to the colonial era.

top_temples.name: Durga Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Serchhip town; built by the local Hindu community, serves as the hub for Navratri/Durga Puja celebrations.
